name: Abu al-Hasan al-Anbari
bio: Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ya'qub was a Baghdad secretary, a Sufi preacher and one of the men whose testimony the courts accepted. He wrote little poetry, but his lament for the vizier Ibn Baqiyya, whose body was displayed in Baghdad in 367 AH (978 CE), circulated widely. Ibn Khallikan quotes Ibn Asakir’s account of how the poet wrote out the elegy and scattered it in the streets of Baghdad, where it passed from reader to reader. Al-Zirikli places his death after 390 AH (1000 CE).
